source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל לְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּצֵ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵל֩ לִקְרַ֨את פְּלִשְׁתִּ֜ים לַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ עַל־הָאֶ֣בֶן הָעֵ֔זֶר וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים חָנ֥וּ בַאֲפֵֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Samuel to all Israel. And went out Israel to meet [the] Philistines for battle, and they camped at the Ebenezer, and [the] Philistines camped at Aphek.

en.L: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. And Israel went out to meet the Philistines for battle, and they camped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
en.B: And the word of Samuel reached all Israel. Now Israel went out to meet the Philistines in battle. The Israelites set up camp at Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
en.R: All Israel heard the messages that Samuel spoke. At that time the Israelites went out to fight against the Philistines. The Israelites camped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.

fr.L: Et la parole de Samuel parvint à tout Israël. Et Israël sortit à la rencontre des Philistins pour le combat, et ils campèrent près d’Eben-Ézer, et les Philistins campèrent à Aphek.
fr.B: La parole de Samuel parvint à tout Israël. Or Israël sortit pour affronter les Philistins. Les Israélites établirent leur camp près d’Eben-Ézer, et les Philistins campèrent à Aphek.
fr.R: Tout Israël a entendu les messages que Samuel annonçait. À cette époque, les Israélites sont partis combattre les Philistins. Ils ont installé leur camp près d’Eben-Ézer, et les Philistins ont installé le leur à Aphek.

decisions.choice: the word of Samuel came to all Israel: the close of the account of Samuel's call
decisions.reason: This first sentence completes 3:19-21: the LORD let none of Samuel's words fall to the ground, and all Israel knew he was a prophet. It does not say that Samuel sent Israel into this battle; in fact Samuel is not mentioned again until chapter 7, and nobody in this chapter asks the LORD's will before fighting.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text, which begins the battle story with "Israel went out"
alternatives: In those days the Philistines gathered for war against Israel, and Israel went out to meet them
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "And it happened in those days that the Philistines gathered for war against Israel, and Israel went out to meet them." That would make the Philistines the attackers. The Hebrew is shorter and is followed here; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: Ebenezer and Aphek: two camps facing each other at the edge of the hill country
decisions.reason: Aphek was a town at the springs of the Yarkon River, where the coastal plain held by the Philistines meets the hills of Ephraim. Ebenezer means "stone of help" and lay somewhere to the east of it; its exact site is unknown. In 7:12 Samuel gives the name Ebenezer to a stone he sets up after a later victory, so the writer may be using the name by which the place came to be known.

decisions.choice: All Israel heard the messages that Samuel spoke
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the word of Samuel" as the prophetic messages Samuel gave (3:19-21), and turns the sentence round so the subject is the people who heard them.

decisions.choice: "Eben-Ézer", "Aphek"
decisions.reason: French writes the name as two words joined by a hyphen, as it is usually written ("stone of help", 7:12), and keeps k for the final consonant of Aphek, as the English; these forms are used through 1 Samuel.

source.text: וַיַּעַרְכ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֜ים לִקְרַ֣את יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַתִּטֹּשׁ֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַיִּנָּ֥גֶף יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לִפְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּכּ֤וּ בַמַּֽעֲרָכָה֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה כְּאַרְבַּ֥עַת אֲלָפִ֖ים אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And drew up [the] Philistines to meet Israel, and spread the battle, and was struck Israel before [the] Philistines, and they struck in the battle line in the field about four thousand men.

en.L: And the Philistines drew up [in line] to meet Israel, and the battle spread, and Israel was struck down before the Philistines; and they struck down in the battle line in the field about 4,000 men.
en.B: The Philistines lined up for battle against Israel, and as the fighting spread, Israel was beaten by the Philistines. They killed about 4,000 men in the ranks out on the open field.
en.R: The Philistines lined up to fight the Israelites. The fighting spread, and the Philistines beat Israel. They killed about 4,000 Israelite soldiers on the battlefield.

fr.L: Et les Philistins se rangèrent [en bataille] à la rencontre d’Israël, et le combat s’étendit, et Israël fut battu devant les Philistins ; et ils frappèrent dans les rangs, en rase campagne, environ quatre mille hommes.
fr.B: Les Philistins se rangèrent en bataille face à Israël ; le combat s’étendit, et Israël fut battu par les Philistins, qui tuèrent dans les rangs, en rase campagne, environ quatre mille hommes.
fr.R: Les Philistins se sont mis en rangs pour attaquer les Israélites. Le combat s’est étendu, et les Philistins ont battu Israël. Ils ont tué environ quatre mille soldats israélites sur le champ de bataille.

decisions.choice: the battle spread: the fighting broke out across the field
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "let go" or "leave", and it is used of raiders spreading out over the land (30:16). Here it seems to describe the battle breaking loose and spreading over the ground between the armies. The exact picture is not certain.

decisions.choice: was struck down: was defeated, with many killed
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of defeat in war and of a blow sent by God. The elders take it up in verse 3 ("Why has the LORD struck us down?"): they see the defeat as the LORD's doing.

decisions.choice: about four thousand: "thousand" as a number
decisions.reason: On the size of numbers given in thousands, see the note at Numbers 1:21; here, as there, the text is read as giving the number.

decisions.choice: Israelite soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says whose men were killed, since the Hebrew leaves the subject and object to be worked out from the sentence.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א הָעָם֮ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֒ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָ֣מָּה נְגָפָ֧נוּ יְהוָ֛ה הַיּ֖וֹם לִפְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים נִקְחָ֧ה אֵלֵ֣ינוּ מִשִּׁלֹ֗ה אֶת־אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְיָבֹ֣א בְקִרְבֵּ֔נוּ וְיֹשִׁעֵ֖נוּ מִכַּ֥ף אֹיְבֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came the people to the camp, and said [the] elders of Israel, Why has struck us Yahweh today before [the] Philistines? Let us take to us from Shiloh [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh, and let it come into our midst and save us from [the] palm of our enemies.

en.L: And the people came to the camp, and the elders of Israel said, "Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck us down today before the Philistines? Let us take to ourselves from Shiloh the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that it may come into our midst and save us from the palm of our enemies."
en.B: When the troops came back to the camp, the elders of Israel said, "Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck us down before the Philistines today? Let us fetch the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from Shiloh. Then it will be among us and will save us from the power of our enemies."
en.R: When the soldiers got back to camp, the leaders of Israel asked, "Why did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make us lose to the Philistines today? Let us bring the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant here from Shiloh. If it is with us, it will save us from our enemies."

fr.L: Et le peuple revint au camp, et les anciens d’Israël dirent : « Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a-t-il battus aujourd’hui devant les Philistins ? Prenons avec nous, de Silo, l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et qu’elle vienne au milieu de nous et nous sauve de la paume de nos ennemis. »
fr.B: Quand les troupes furent revenues au camp, les anciens d’Israël dirent : « Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a-t-il laissés battre aujourd’hui par les Philistins ? Allons chercher à Silo l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Elle sera au milieu de nous et nous sauvera du pouvoir de nos ennemis. »
fr.R: Quand les soldats sont revenus au camp, les chefs d’Israël ont demandé : « Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a-t-il fait perdre contre les Philistins aujourd’hui ? Allons chercher à Silo l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Si elle est avec nous, elle nous sauvera de nos ennemis. »

decisions.choice: Why has the LORD struck us down: the elders see the defeat as the LORD's act
decisions.reason: They rightly understand that the LORD has given the victory to the Philistines, but they do not ask him why or turn back to him. Instead they decide to carry his ark into battle, as if its presence would force a different result.

decisions.choice: the ark of the covenant: the sacred chest that stood for the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: The ark was the gold-covered chest that held the tablets of the covenant (Exodus 25:10-22; Deuteronomy 10:1-5). It was kept at Shiloh in the house of the LORD, where Samuel slept near it (3:3). It had gone ahead of Israel across the Jordan and around Jericho (Joshua 3-6).

decisions.choice: it may come ... and save us: the ark is the subject
alternatives: that he may come among us and save us
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular and follow straight after "the ark", so the ark is most naturally their subject. They could also be read of the LORD himself ("that he may come among us and save us"). Either way the elders expect the ark to bring the LORD's saving power with it, as though it were a charm.

decisions.choice: from the palm of our enemies: from our enemies' power
decisions.reason: "Palm" or "hand" stands for power and control, as often (Judges 6:14).

decisions.choice: troops (Balanced); soldiers, leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The people" here means the men who had fought, so Balanced says "troops" and Readable "soldiers". Readable calls the elders "leaders", the plainer word.

decisions.choice: make us lose to the Philistines
decisions.reason: Readable puts "struck us down before the Philistines" in plain words while keeping the LORD as the one who caused the defeat.

decisions.choice: "nous a-t-il laissés battre"
decisions.reason: The elders see the defeat as the LORD's act (m1); French "frapper" with a people as object sounds like a physical blow, so Balanced says that the LORD let them be beaten, keeping him as the one who acts.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח הָעָם֙ שִׁלֹ֔ה וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֗ם אֵ֣ת אֲר֧וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַכְּרֻבִ֑ים וְשָׁ֞ם שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־עֵלִ֗י עִם־אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים חָפְנִ֖י וּפִֽינְחָֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the people [to] Shiloh, and they carried from there [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh of hosts, sitting [on] the cherubim; and there [were the] two sons of Eli with [the] ark of [the] covenant of the God, Hophni and Phinehas.

en.L: And the people sent to Shiloh, and they carried from there the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, who sits [on] the cherubim. And there [were] the two sons of Eli with the ark of the covenant of God, Hophni and Phinehas.
en.B: So the people sent word to Shiloh, and from there they carried away the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, who sits enthroned on the cherubim. And Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, accompanied the ark of the covenant of God.
en.R: So the people sent men to Shiloh to fetch the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. He sits as king above the cherubim, the winged creatures on the lid of the ark. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of God's covenant.

fr.L: Et le peuple envoya à Silo, et ils emportèrent de là l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} des armées, qui siège [sur] les chérubins. Et là [étaient] les deux fils d’Éli avec l’arche de l’alliance de Dieu, Hophni et Phinéas.
fr.B: Le peuple envoya donc des hommes à Silo, et l’on rapporta de là l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} des armées, qui siège sur les chérubins. Les deux fils d’Éli, Hophni et Phinéas, accompagnaient l’arche de l’alliance de Dieu.
fr.R: Alors le peuple a envoyé des hommes à Silo pour chercher l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} des armées. Il siège comme un roi au-dessus des chérubins, les êtres ailés qui sont sur le couvercle de l’arche. Les deux fils d’Éli, Hophni et Phinéas, étaient là avec l’arche de l’alliance de Dieu.

decisions.choice: the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts who sits enthroned on the cherubim: the full title of the God of the ark
decisions.reason: "The LORD of hosts" names him as the commander of armies, the armies of heaven and of Israel; the title is first used in this book of the worship at Shiloh (1:3, 11). The ark's cover had two gold cherubim with wings spread over it (Exodus 25:18-22), and the LORD was pictured as seated above them as on a throne, with the ark as his footstool (Psalm 80:2; 99:1; 1 Chronicles 28:2). The writer gives the title in full here, so that the reader feels what is at stake when this ark goes into battle and is lost.

decisions.choice: sits: sits enthroned, reigns
decisions.reason: The verb means "sit" or "dwell"; of a king it means to sit on a throne. With "the cherubim" it pictures the LORD as king seated above them.

decisions.choice: Eli's two sons with the ark: the priests already under judgment
decisions.reason: Hophni and Phinehas were the priests who robbed the offerings and abused their office (2:12-17, 22-25). A man of God had told Eli that both would die on one day as a sign (2:34). Naming them beside the ark warns the reader what is coming.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: As everywhere in these books, Balanced and Readable say "Armies" for "hosts", the plainer word for what the title means; Literal keeps "hosts".

decisions.choice: sits as king above the cherubim, the winged creatures on the lid of the ark
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the cherubim were and where they were, as Isaiah 37:16 does, so the reader can see the picture of the LORD's throne. It starts a new sentence for the title.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כְּב֨וֹא אֲר֤וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָה֙ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיָּרִ֥עוּ כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תְּרוּעָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַתֵּהֹ֖ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when came [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh into the camp, and shouted all Israel [a] great shout, and resounded the earth.

en.L: And it was, when the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came into the camp, all Israel shouted a great shout, and the earth resounded.
en.B: As the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} reached the camp, all Israel raised such a great shout that the ground shook.
en.R: When the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant came into the camp, all the Israelites gave a great shout. It was so loud that the ground shook.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} entra dans le camp, que tout Israël poussa une grande clameur, et la terre en retentit.
fr.B: Quand l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} arriva au camp, tout Israël poussa une si grande clameur que le sol en trembla.
fr.R: Quand l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est entrée dans le camp, tous les Israélites ont poussé un grand cri. Il était si fort que le sol a tremblé.

decisions.choice: a great shout: the war cry
decisions.reason: The word is the loud shout raised for battle and in welcome of the LORD's presence. Israel shouted as the walls of Jericho fell (Joshua 6:5, 20), and David's people shouted as the ark was brought to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:15). Here the shout is full of confidence, which the story is about to overturn.

decisions.choice: the earth resounded: the noise echoed until the ground seemed to shake
decisions.reason: The verb means to be in an uproar or to be stirred up (Ruth 1:19; 1 Kings 1:45). It describes noise so great that the land itself seemed to shake with it.

decisions.choice: the ground shook
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the effect of the noise with a familiar picture; Literal keeps "the earth resounded".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמְע֤וּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ אֶת־ק֣וֹל הַתְּרוּעָ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֶ֠ה ק֣וֹל הַתְּרוּעָ֧ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֛ה הַזֹּ֖את בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה הָעִבְרִ֑ים וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֚י אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה בָּ֖א אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard [the] Philistines the sound of the shout, and they said, What [is] the sound of the great shout the this in [the] camp of the Hebrews? And they knew that [the] ark of Yahweh had come into the camp.

en.L: And the Philistines heard the sound of the shout, and they said, "What [is] the sound of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews?" And they learned that the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had come into the camp.
en.B: When the Philistines heard the noise of the shouting, they asked, "What is this great shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?" Then they found out that the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had come into the camp.
en.R: The Philistines heard the noise and asked, "Why are the Hebrews shouting so loudly in their camp?" Then they found out that the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had come there.

fr.L: Et les Philistins entendirent le bruit de la clameur, et ils dirent : « Qu’[est] le bruit de cette grande clameur dans le camp des Hébreux ? » Et ils surent que l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} était arrivée au camp.
fr.B: En entendant le bruit de cette clameur, les Philistins demandèrent : « Que signifie cette grande clameur dans le camp des Hébreux ? » Puis ils apprirent que l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} était arrivée au camp.
fr.R: Les Philistins ont entendu le bruit et ont demandé : « Pourquoi les Hébreux crient-ils si fort dans leur camp ? » Ensuite, ils ont appris que l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} était arrivée là-bas.

decisions.choice: the Hebrews: the name others used for the Israelites
decisions.reason: Foreigners call Israel "the Hebrews", often with contempt (Genesis 39:14; Exodus 1:15-16; 1 Samuel 13:19; 14:11). The Philistines use it three times in this scene (verses 6 and 9).

decisions.choice: they knew: they came to know, found out
decisions.reason: The verb describes learning something they did not know before; perhaps scouts or prisoners told them.

decisions.choice: Why are the Hebrews shouting so loudly
decisions.reason: Readable puts the Philistines' question as a plain question about the shouting, keeping its sense.

source.text: וַיִּֽרְאוּ֙ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים כִּ֣י אָמְר֔וּ בָּ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיֹּאמְרוּ֙ א֣וֹי לָ֔נוּ כִּ֣י לֹ֥א הָיְתָ֛ה כָּזֹ֖את אֶתְמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֹֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And were afraid the Philistines, for they said, God has come into the camp. And they said, Woe to us! For not has been like this yesterday [and] three days ago.

en.L: And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, "A god has come into the camp." And they said, "Woe to us! For [anything] like this has not happened yesterday [or the day] before.
en.B: The Philistines were afraid, because they said, "A god has come into the camp." And they said, "Woe to us! Nothing like this has ever happened before.
en.R: The Philistines were frightened. They said, "A god has come into their camp!" And they said, "We are doomed! Nothing like this has ever happened before.

fr.L: Et les Philistins eurent peur, car ils dirent : « Un dieu est venu dans le camp. » Et ils dirent : « Malheur à nous ! Car rien de pareil n’est arrivé hier [ni] avant-hier.
fr.B: Les Philistins eurent peur, car ils se disaient : « Un dieu est venu dans le camp. » Et ils ajoutaient : « Malheur à nous ! Jamais rien de pareil n’est arrivé jusqu’ici.
fr.R: Les Philistins ont eu peur. Ils disaient : « Un dieu est venu dans leur camp ! » Et ils disaient aussi : « Nous sommes perdus ! Rien de pareil n’est jamais arrivé.

decisions.choice: a god has come: the Philistines speak of a divine being arriving
alternatives: God has come into the camp
decisions.reason: The word for God has a singular verb, as it usually does when it means the God of Israel, so the sentence could be read "God has come into the camp". But these are Philistines speaking, and in the next verse they speak of "these mighty gods" in the plural; they mean that a god has come to fight for Israel. Either way, they treat the ark as the god's arrival.

decisions.choice: yesterday and the day before: in the past, ever before
decisions.reason: "Yesterday and three days ago" is a Hebrew way of saying "before now" (Genesis 31:2; Exodus 5:8).

decisions.choice: We are doomed
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the cry "Woe to us!" means. The quotation continues to the end of verse 9.

source.text: א֣וֹי לָ֔נוּ מִ֣י יַצִּילֵ֔נוּ מִיַּ֛ד הָאֱלֹהִ֥ים הָאַדִּירִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה אֵ֧לֶּה הֵ֣ם הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים הַמַּכִּ֧ים אֶת־מִצְרַ֛יִם בְּכָל־מַכָּ֖ה בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe to us! Who will deliver us from [the] hand of the gods the mighty the these? These [are] the gods striking Egypt with every plague in the wilderness.

en.L: Woe to us! Who will rescue us from the hand of these mighty gods? These [are] the gods who struck Egypt with every [kind of] plague in the wilderness.
en.B: Woe to us! Who will rescue us from the power of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck down the Egyptians with every kind of plague in the wilderness.
en.R: We are doomed! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of disasters in the desert.

fr.L: Malheur à nous ! Qui nous délivrera de la main de ces dieux puissants ? Ce [sont] les dieux qui ont frappé l’Égypte de toutes [sortes de] fléaux dans le désert.
fr.B: Malheur à nous ! Qui nous délivrera du pouvoir de ces dieux puissants ? Ce sont ces dieux-là qui ont frappé les Égyptiens de toutes sortes de fléaux dans le désert.
fr.R: Nous sommes perdus ! Qui pourra nous sauver de ces dieux puissants ? Ce sont les dieux qui ont frappé les Égyptiens par toutes sortes de malheurs dans le désert.

decisions.choice: these mighty gods: Israel's God spoken of in the plural
decisions.reason: The noun, the adjective and the verb are all plural. The Philistines worshiped many gods, and they speak of Israel's God as a band of gods. The writer lets their words show how little they understand him.

decisions.choice: the gods who struck Egypt: the plagues of the exodus
decisions.reason: The story of the LORD's blows against Egypt (Exodus 7-12) was known among the nations (Joshua 2:10; 9:9), and the Philistines will recall it again in 6:6.

decisions.choice: in the wilderness: as the Hebrew reads
alternatives: with every plague, and in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The plagues fell on Egypt, not in the wilderness. The Philistines may be running together the plagues and what followed in the wilderness, such as the drowning of Egypt's army at the sea; a foreign people's account need not be exact. The ancient Greek translation reads "and in the wilderness", as if the wilderness events were a second item. The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: disasters; desert
decisions.reason: Readable uses "disasters" for the plagues and "desert", the everyday word for the wilderness.

source.text: הִֽתְחַזְּק֞וּ וִֽהְי֤וּ לַֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים פֶּ֚ן תַּעַבְד֣וּ לָעִבְרִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָבְד֖וּ לָכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶ֥ם לַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים וְנִלְחַמְתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Show yourselves strong and be for men, Philistines, lest you serve [the] Hebrews as they served you; and be for men and fight.

en.L: Be strong and be men, Philistines, so that you do not serve the Hebrews as they have served you. Be men and fight!"
en.B: Be strong, Philistines, and act like men, or you will become slaves of the Hebrews as they have been slaves to you. Act like men and fight!"
en.R: Be strong, Philistines! Be brave men! If you are not, you will be slaves of the Hebrews, the way they have been your slaves. So be brave and fight!"

fr.L: Soyez forts et soyez des hommes, Philistins, pour que vous ne serviez pas les Hébreux comme ils vous ont servis. Soyez des hommes et combattez ! »
fr.B: Courage, Philistins, conduisez-vous en hommes, sinon vous deviendrez les esclaves des Hébreux comme ils ont été les vôtres. Conduisez-vous en hommes et combattez ! »
fr.R: Soyez forts, Philistins ! Soyez courageux ! Sinon, vous deviendrez les esclaves des Hébreux, comme eux ont été vos esclaves. Alors soyez courageux et battez-vous ! »

decisions.choice: be men: show the courage expected of fighting men
decisions.reason: The same call is heard in 2 Samuel 10:12 and 1 Kings 2:2. The Philistines urge one another not to lose heart in spite of their fear.

decisions.choice: serve the Hebrews as they served you: be ruled by Israel as Israel was ruled by the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Philistines had ruled over Israel since the days of Samson (Judges 13:1; 15:11), taking tribute and labor. The verb "serve" here means to be subject to another people. They fear the roles will be reversed.

decisions.choice: become slaves of the Hebrews (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: The point is one people held in subjection by another, so Balanced and Readable say "slaves" rather than the softer "serve"; Literal keeps the verb "serve".

source.text: וַיִּלָּחֲמ֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיִּנָּ֤גֶף יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיָּנֻ֨סוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְאֹהָלָ֔יו וַתְּהִ֥י הַמַּכָּ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיִּפֹּל֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף רַגְלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And fought [the] Philistines, and was struck Israel, and they fled each to his tents; and was the slaughter great very, and fell from Israel thirty thousand foot soldier[s].

en.L: And the Philistines fought, and Israel was struck down, and they fled, each man to his tents. And the slaughter was very great, and 30,000 foot soldiers of Israel fell.
en.B: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and every man fled to his home. The slaughter was very great: 30,000 of Israel's foot soldiers fell.
en.R: So the Philistines fought, and Israel lost the battle. Every Israelite soldier ran away to his own home. Very many were killed. Israel lost 30,000 soldiers who fought on foot.

fr.L: Et les Philistins combattirent, et Israël fut battu, et ils s’enfuirent chacun à ses tentes. Et la défaite fut très grande, et il tomba d’Israël trente mille fantassins.
fr.B: Les Philistins combattirent donc, et Israël fut battu ; chacun s’enfuit chez soi. Ce fut un très grand massacre : trente mille fantassins d’Israël tombèrent.
fr.R: Alors les Philistins ont attaqué, et Israël a perdu la bataille. Chaque soldat israélite s’est enfui chez lui. Il y a eu beaucoup de morts : Israël a perdu trente mille soldats qui combattaient à pied.

decisions.choice: fled each to his tents: the army broke up and every man ran home
decisions.reason: "To his tents" means "home", a phrase left over from the time when Israel lived in tents (2 Samuel 18:17; 1 Kings 12:16). Israel's army no longer existed as a fighting force.

decisions.choice: thirty thousand: "thousand" as a number
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the text is read as giving the number. On the word "thousand", which can also name a unit of a tribe or army, see the note at Numbers 1:21.

decisions.choice: foot soldiers: men who fought on foot
decisions.reason: Israel had no chariots or horsemen at this time; its army was made up of men on foot.

decisions.choice: to his home
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of "to his tents" (m1), which in English would suggest a soldier's tent in camp.

source.text: וַאֲר֥וֹן אֱלֹהִ֖ים נִלְקָ֑ח וּשְׁנֵ֤י בְנֵֽי־עֵלִי֙ מֵ֔תוּ חָפְנִ֖י וּפִֽינְחָֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] ark of God was taken, and [the] two sons of Eli died, Hophni and Phinehas.

en.L: And the ark of God was taken, and the two sons of Eli died, Hophni and Phinehas.
en.B: The ark of God was captured, and both of Eli's sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
en.R: The Philistines captured the ark of God. And Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were killed.

fr.L: Et l’arche de Dieu fut prise, et les deux fils d’Éli moururent, Hophni et Phinéas.
fr.B: L’arche de Dieu fut prise, et les deux fils d’Éli, Hophni et Phinéas, moururent.
fr.R: Les Philistins ont pris l’arche de Dieu. Et les deux fils d’Éli, Hophni et Phinéas, ont été tués.

decisions.choice: the ark of God was taken: the loss of the ark comes first
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "the ark" at the front of the sentence, before the deaths of the priests. The capture of the ark is the center of the disaster, and the rest of the chapter returns to it again and again (verses 13, 17, 18, 19, 21, 22). From here on the writer calls it "the ark of God".

decisions.choice: Eli's two sons died: the sign given to Eli comes true
decisions.reason: A man of God had told Eli that Hophni and Phinehas would die on the same day (2:34), and the LORD had told Samuel that he would carry out everything he had said against Eli's house (3:11-14).

decisions.choice: The Philistines captured; were killed
decisions.reason: Readable names who took the ark and says how the two men died, both of which the context makes plain.

source.text: וַיָּ֤רָץ אִישׁ־בִּנְיָמִן֙ מֵהַמַּ֣עֲרָכָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א שִׁלֹ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וּמַדָּ֣יו קְרֻעִ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And ran [a] man of Benjamin from the battle line and came [to] Shiloh on the day the that, and his clothes [were] torn, and earth [was] on his head.

en.L: And a man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh on that day, and his clothes [were] torn, and earth [was] on his head.
en.B: A man of the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battle line and reached Shiloh that same day. His clothes were torn, and there was dirt on his head.
en.R: A man from the tribe of Benjamin ran all the way from the battle to Shiloh that same day. His clothes were torn, and there was dirt on his head to show his sorrow.

fr.L: Et un homme de Benjamin courut de la ligne de bataille et arriva à Silo ce jour-là, et ses vêtements [étaient] déchirés, et de la terre [était] sur sa tête.
fr.B: Un homme de la tribu de Benjamin s’échappa du combat en courant et arriva à Silo le jour même. Il avait les vêtements déchirés et de la terre sur la tête.
fr.R: Un homme de la tribu de Benjamin a couru depuis le champ de bataille jusqu’à Silo, le jour même. Ses vêtements étaient déchirés, et il avait mis de la terre sur sa tête pour montrer sa tristesse.

decisions.choice: torn clothes and earth on the head: signs of mourning
decisions.reason: People tore their clothes and threw dust or earth on their heads at news of death or disaster (Joshua 7:6; 2 Samuel 1:2; 15:32). Before the runner says a word, the people of Shiloh can see that he brings bad news.

decisions.choice: on that day: a long run through the hills
decisions.reason: The road from Aphek on the plain up to Shiloh in the hill country of Ephraim is a long day's journey on foot. The runner covers it on the day of the battle, so the news reaches Shiloh before anyone else.

decisions.choice: of the tribe of Benjamin
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that Benjamin is a tribe; Readable also adds what the torn clothes and the dirt meant (m1).

source.text: וַיָּב֗וֹא וְהִנֵּ֣ה עֵ֠לִי יֹשֵׁ֨ב עַֽל־הַכִּסֵּ֜א יַ֥ד דֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ מְצַפֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־הָיָ֤ה לִבּוֹ֙ חָרֵ֔ד עַ֖ל אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְהָאִ֗ישׁ בָּ֚א לְהַגִּ֣יד בָּעִ֔יר וַתִּזְעַ֖ק כָּל־הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he came, and look, Eli [was] sitting on the seat beside [the] road watching, for was his heart trembling for [the] ark of the God. And the man came to tell in the city, and cried out all the city.

en.L: And he came, and look, Eli [was] sitting on the seat beside the road, watching, for his heart was trembling for the ark of God. And the man came to tell [it] in the city, and all the city cried out.
en.B: When he arrived, there was Eli sitting on his seat beside the road, watching, because his heart trembled for the ark of God. The man came to tell the news in the town, and the whole town cried out.
en.R: When he got there, Eli was sitting on his chair by the side of the road, watching. He was very worried about the ark of God. The man went into the town and told what had happened, and everyone in the town cried out.

fr.L: Et il arriva, et voici, Éli [était] assis sur le siège au bord du chemin, guettant, car son cœur tremblait pour l’arche de Dieu. Et l’homme vint annoncer [la nouvelle] dans la ville, et toute la ville poussa des cris.
fr.B: Quand il arriva, Éli était assis sur son siège au bord du chemin et guettait, car son cœur tremblait pour l’arche de Dieu. L’homme vint annoncer la nouvelle dans la ville, et toute la ville se mit à crier.
fr.R: Quand il est arrivé, Éli était assis sur sa chaise au bord de la route et il guettait. Il était très inquiet pour l’arche de Dieu. L’homme est entré dans la ville et il a raconté ce qui s’était passé. Alors tous les habitants de la ville ont poussé des cris.

decisions.choice: beside the road: the word as the Hebrew tradition reads it aloud
alternatives: beside the gate, watching the road
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has a form that makes no clear sense here, and the tradition of reading the text aloud gives the word "beside" (literally "hand", meaning "side"), the same word as in verse 18, "beside the gate". The reading tradition is followed. The ancient Greek translation reads "beside the gate, watching the road", which agrees with verse 18.

decisions.choice: watching: looking out, waiting for news
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a watchman on the lookout (2 Samuel 18:24-27). Eli could no longer see (verse 15), so the word describes his waiting and straining for news rather than what his eyes could take in.

decisions.choice: his heart was trembling for the ark: he was full of fear for the ark
decisions.reason: "Heart" is the seat of thought and feeling. The old priest's fear is for the ark of God first; it is the news of the ark, not of his sons, that kills him (verse 18).

decisions.choice: He was very worried about the ark of God
decisions.reason: Readable puts the picture of a trembling heart into plain words.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע עֵלִי֙ אֶת־ק֣וֹל הַצְּעָקָ֔ה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מֶ֛ה ק֥וֹל הֶהָמ֖וֹן הַזֶּ֑ה וְהָאִ֣ישׁ מִהַ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֖א וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לְעֵלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Eli the sound of the outcry, and he said, What [is] the sound of the uproar the this? And the man hurried and came and told Eli.

en.L: And Eli heard the sound of the outcry, and he said, "What [is] the sound of this uproar?" And the man hurried and came and told Eli.
en.B: When Eli heard the sound of the outcry, he asked, "What is the sound of this uproar?" The man hurried over and told Eli.
en.R: Eli heard the people crying out. He asked, "What is all this noise?" The man hurried over to Eli and told him the news.

fr.L: Et Éli entendit le bruit des cris, et il dit : « Qu’[est] le bruit de ce tumulte ? » Et l’homme se hâta et vint et informa Éli.
fr.B: Éli entendit les cris et demanda : « Que signifie ce tumulte ? » L’homme se hâta de venir annoncer la nouvelle à Éli.
fr.R: Éli a entendu les gens crier. Il a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que c’est que tout ce bruit ? » L’homme s’est dépêché d’aller vers Éli et lui a annoncé la nouvelle.

decisions.choice: What is the sound of this uproar? an echo of the Philistines' question
decisions.reason: In verse 6 the Philistines asked, "What is the sound of this great shout?" when Israel cheered the ark. Now Eli asks the same kind of question about a cry of grief. The joyful shout has turned into wailing.

decisions.choice: told Eli: the report itself is given in verses 16-17
decisions.reason: Verse 15 pauses to describe Eli's age and blindness before the conversation is given.

source.text: וְעֵלִ֕י בֶּן־תִּשְׁעִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנֶ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה וְעֵינָ֣יו קָ֔מָה וְלֹ֥א יָכ֖וֹל לִרְאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And Eli [was a] son of ninety and eight year[s], and his eyes stood, and not he could see.

en.L: Now Eli [was] ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were set, and he could not see.
en.B: Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were fixed, so that he could not see.
en.R: Eli was ninety-eight years old. His eyes no longer moved, and he was blind.

fr.L: Or Éli [était] âgé de quatre-vingt-dix-huit ans, et ses yeux étaient fixes, et il ne pouvait pas voir.
fr.B: Éli avait quatre-vingt-dix-huit ans ; ses yeux étaient fixes, et il ne voyait plus.
fr.R: Éli avait quatre-vingt-dix-huit ans. Ses yeux ne bougeaient plus, et il était aveugle.

decisions.choice: a son of ninety-eight years: ninety-eight years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: his eyes were set: his eyes had become fixed and blind
decisions.reason: The verb means "stand". Eyes that "stand" no longer move or see (1 Kings 14:4, of the old prophet Ahijah). Eli's sight had been growing dim (3:2); now he was fully blind, which is why he had to ask what the noise was.

decisions.choice: His eyes no longer moved, and he was blind
decisions.reason: Readable explains "his eyes were set" in everyday words.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָאִ֜ישׁ אֶל־עֵלִ֗י אָֽנֹכִי֙ הַבָּ֣א מִן־הַמַּעֲרָכָ֔ה וַאֲנִ֕י מִן־הַמַּעֲרָכָ֖ה נַ֣סְתִּי הַיּ֑וֹם וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מֶֽה־הָיָ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the man to Eli, I [am] the [one] coming from the battle line, and I from the battle line fled today. And he said, What was the matter, my son?

en.L: And the man said to Eli, "I [am] the one who came from the battle line, and I fled from the battle line today." And he said, "What was the matter, my son?"
en.B: The man said to Eli, "I am the one who has come from the battle. I fled from the battle line today." Eli asked, "What happened, my son?"
en.R: The man said to Eli, "I have just come from the battle. I ran away from the fighting today." Eli asked, "What happened, my son?"

fr.L: Et l’homme dit à Éli : « C’est moi qui viens de la ligne de bataille, et c’est moi qui me suis enfui de la ligne de bataille aujourd’hui. » Et il dit : « Qu’est-il arrivé, mon fils ? »
fr.B: L’homme dit à Éli : « J’arrive du combat. Je me suis enfui du champ de bataille aujourd’hui même. » Éli demanda : « Que s’est-il passé, mon fils ? »
fr.R: L’homme a dit à Éli : « J’arrive tout juste de la bataille. Je me suis enfui du combat aujourd’hui. » Éli a demandé : « Que s’est-il passé, mon fils ? »

decisions.choice: What was the matter? What happened? How did it go?
decisions.reason: David asks the same question of the messenger who brings news of Saul's death (2 Samuel 1:4).

decisions.choice: my son: a kindly way for an older man to address a younger one
decisions.reason: The runner is not Eli's son; Eli speaks to him as an old man to a young one, as he spoke to Samuel (3:6, 16).

decisions.choice: the battle (first mention)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the battle" the first time for "the battle line" and keep the line only where it reads naturally, to avoid repeating the same phrase in two short sentences.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַן הַֽמְבַשֵּׂ֜ר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָ֤ס יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְגַ֛ם מַגֵּפָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה הָיְתָ֣ה בָעָ֑ם וְגַם־שְׁנֵ֨י בָנֶ֜יךָ מֵ֗תוּ חָפְנִי֙ וּפִ֣ינְחָ֔ס וַאֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים נִלְקָֽחָה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And answered the one bringing news and said, Fled Israel before [the] Philistines, and also [a] slaughter great has been among the people, and also two sons of yours died, Hophni and Phinehas, and [the] ark of the God has been taken.

en.L: And the one bringing the news answered and said, "Israel has fled before the Philistines, and also there has been a great slaughter among the people, and also your two sons are dead, Hophni and Phinehas, and the ark of God has been taken."
en.B: The messenger answered, "Israel fled from the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the troops. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead too, and the ark of God has been captured."
en.R: The man who brought the news answered, "Israel ran away from the Philistines. Many of our soldiers were killed. Both your sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead. And the Philistines have captured the ark of God!"

fr.L: Et celui qui apportait la nouvelle répondit et dit : « Israël a fui devant les Philistins, et il y a eu aussi une grande défaite parmi le peuple, et aussi tes deux fils sont morts, Hophni et Phinéas, et l’arche de Dieu a été prise. »
fr.B: Le messager répondit : « Israël a fui devant les Philistins, et l’armée a subi de lourdes pertes. Tes deux fils, Hophni et Phinéas, sont morts eux aussi, et l’arche de Dieu a été prise. »
fr.R: L’homme qui apportait la nouvelle a répondu : « Israël s’est enfui devant les Philistins. Beaucoup de nos soldats ont été tués. Tes deux fils, Hophni et Phinéas, sont morts. Et les Philistins ont pris l’arche de Dieu ! »

decisions.choice: the one bringing news: a messenger, usually of good news
decisions.reason: The word is used of one who brings tidings, most often good news of victory (2 Samuel 18:19-20, 26; Isaiah 52:7). Here the bearer of tidings brings the worst news possible.

decisions.choice: and also ... and also ... and the ark: a report that builds to its worst point
decisions.reason: The messenger gives four pieces of news, each one heavier than the last: the defeat, the great loss of life, the death of Eli's sons, and last of all the capture of the ark.

decisions.choice: slaughter: a crushing defeat with great loss of life
decisions.reason: The word means a blow or a plague, often one sent by God (Numbers 14:37; 2 Samuel 24:21). Here it is the heavy losses of the battle (verse 10).

decisions.choice: the Philistines have captured
decisions.reason: Readable names who took the ark, as in verse 11.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י כְּהַזְכִּיר֣וֹ׀אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים וַיִּפֹּ֣ל מֵֽעַל־הַ֠כִּסֵּא אֲחֹ֨רַנִּ֜ית בְּעַ֣ד׀יַ֣ד הַשַּׁ֗עַר וַתִּשָּׁבֵ֤ר מַפְרַקְתּוֹ֙ וַיָּמֹ֔ת כִּֽי־זָקֵ֥ן הָאִ֖ישׁ וְכָבֵ֑ד וְה֛וּא שָׁפַ֥ט אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when he mentioned [the] ark of the God, and he fell from on the seat backward beside [the] side of the gate, and was broken his neck and he died, for old [was] the man and heavy; and he judged Israel forty year[s].

en.L: And it was, when he mentioned the ark of God, [Eli] fell from the seat backward beside the gate, and his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.
en.B: As soon as the man mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell backward from his seat beside the gate. His neck broke and he died, since he was old and heavy. For forty years he had judged Israel.
en.R: When the man spoke about the ark of God, Eli fell backward off his chair beside the gate. His neck was broken and he died, because he was old and heavy. Eli had led Israel for forty years.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand il mentionna l’arche de Dieu, [qu’Éli] tomba de son siège à la renverse, à côté de la porte, et sa nuque se brisa et il mourut, car l’homme était vieux et lourd. Et il avait jugé Israël quarante ans.
fr.B: Dès que l’homme eut mentionné l’arche de Dieu, Éli tomba de son siège à la renverse, à côté de la porte. Il se brisa la nuque et mourut, car il était vieux et lourd. Il avait jugé Israël pendant quarante ans.
fr.R: Quand l’homme a parlé de l’arche de Dieu, Éli est tombé de sa chaise à la renverse, à côté de la porte. Il s’est cassé le cou et il est mort, car il était vieux et lourd. Éli avait dirigé Israël pendant quarante ans.

decisions.choice: when he mentioned the ark of God: it is the news of the ark that brings Eli down
decisions.reason: Eli hears of the defeat and of his sons' deaths, but it is at the word "ark" that he falls. His heart had trembled for the ark (verse 13).

decisions.choice: heavy: a word from the same root as "glory" and "honor"
decisions.reason: Eli had honored his sons more than the LORD and made himself fat on the best of the offerings (2:29); the LORD had said, "Those who honor me I will honor" (2:30). The "heavy" old priest dies on the day the glory leaves Israel (verses 21-22), and the words echo one another.

decisions.choice: judged Israel: led Israel as judge
decisions.reason: As in the book of Judges (see Judges 2:16), to "judge" Israel means to lead and govern it, not only to settle disputes. Eli is counted as the last of the judges before Samuel (7:15).

decisions.choice: forty years: as the Hebrew reads
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "twenty years". The Hebrew is followed; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: Eli
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he" for both the man who mentioned the ark and the one who fell. English names Eli as the one who fell (in brackets at Literal), and Balanced and Readable name "the man" as the one who spoke.

decisions.choice: led Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "led", as it does for the judges (m3).

source.text: וְכַלָּת֣וֹ אֵֽשֶׁת־פִּינְחָס֮ הָרָ֣ה לָלַת֒ וַתִּשְׁמַ֣ע אֶת־הַשְּׁמֻעָ֔ה אֶל־הִלָּקַח֙ אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּמֵ֥ת חָמִ֖יהָ וְאִישָׁ֑הּ וַתִּכְרַ֣ע וַתֵּ֔לֶד כִּֽי־נֶהֶפְכ֥וּ עָלֶ֖יהָ צִרֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And his daughter-in-law, [the] wife of Phinehas, [was] pregnant, to give birth. And she heard the report about [the] taking of [the] ark of the God and [that] had died her father-in-law and her husband, and she crouched and gave birth, for turned upon her her pains.

en.L: And his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, [was] pregnant, about to give birth. And when she heard the news that the ark of God was taken and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, she crouched down and gave birth, for her pains turned upon her.
en.B: Now his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and near the time of giving birth. When she heard the news that the ark of God had been captured and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, she crouched down and gave birth, for her labor pains came on her suddenly.
en.R: Eli's daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant, and her baby was almost due. She heard that the ark of God had been captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead. Then her labor pains suddenly began. She crouched down and gave birth.

fr.L: Et sa belle-fille, la femme de Phinéas, [était] enceinte, sur le point d’accoucher. Et elle entendit la nouvelle que l’arche de Dieu était prise, et que son beau-père et son mari étaient morts, et elle se courba et accoucha, car ses douleurs fondirent sur elle.
fr.B: Or sa belle-fille, la femme de Phinéas, était enceinte et près d’accoucher. Quand elle apprit que l’arche de Dieu avait été prise et que son beau-père et son mari étaient morts, elle se courba et accoucha, car les douleurs la saisirent brusquement.
fr.R: La belle-fille d’Éli, la femme de Phinéas, était enceinte, et son bébé devait bientôt naître. Elle a appris que l’arche de Dieu avait été prise, et que son beau-père et son mari étaient morts. Alors les douleurs de l’accouchement ont commencé tout à coup. Elle s’est accroupie et elle a mis son enfant au monde.

decisions.choice: the taking of the ark ... her father-in-law and her husband: the ark named first
decisions.reason: As in the messenger's report and Eli's death, the capture of the ark comes first in what she hears.

decisions.choice: her pains turned upon her: labor came on her suddenly and overwhelmed her
decisions.reason: The verb means "turn" or "be overturned". The shock of the news brought on labor at once, and the pains came on her with sudden force.

decisions.choice: she crouched: the position for giving birth
decisions.reason: The verb means to kneel or crouch down; women in this culture often gave birth kneeling or crouching.

decisions.choice: her labor pains came on her suddenly
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of "her pains turned upon her" (m2).

source.text: וּכְעֵ֣ת מוּתָ֗הּ וַתְּדַבֵּ֨רְנָה֙ הַנִּצָּב֣וֹת עָלֶ֔יהָ אַל־תִּֽירְאִ֖י כִּ֣י בֵ֣ן יָלָ֑דְתְּ וְלֹ֥א עָנְתָ֖ה וְלֹא־שָׁ֥תָה לִבָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And about [the] time of her dying, and spoke the [women] standing over her, Not fear, for [a] son you have borne. And not she answered, and not she set her heart.

en.L: And about the time of her death, the [women] standing over her said, "Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son." But she did not answer, and she did not set her heart [to it].
en.B: As she was dying, the women who stood beside her said, "Do not be afraid; you have given birth to a son." But she did not answer or pay any attention.
en.R: She was dying. The women who were helping her said, "Do not be afraid. You have a baby boy!" But she did not answer them. She did not even seem to notice.

fr.L: Et vers le moment de sa mort, les [femmes] qui se tenaient auprès d’elle dirent : « Ne crains pas, car tu as enfanté un fils. » Mais elle ne répondit pas et n’y prêta pas son cœur.
fr.B: Comme elle était en train de mourir, les femmes qui l’assistaient lui dirent : « N’aie pas peur, tu as mis au monde un fils. » Mais elle ne répondit rien et n’y prêta aucune attention.
fr.R: Elle était en train de mourir. Les femmes qui l’aidaient lui ont dit : « N’aie pas peur. Tu as un petit garçon ! » Mais elle ne leur a pas répondu. Elle n’a même pas semblé entendre.

decisions.choice: Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son: words of comfort to a dying mother
decisions.reason: The midwife spoke almost the same words to Rachel as she died giving birth to Benjamin (Genesis 35:17-18). A son was news meant to cheer, but Phinehas's wife has lost too much to take comfort in it.

decisions.choice: the women standing over her: the women attending the birth
decisions.reason: The word is a feminine plural, "those standing". They were the women, perhaps midwives, who helped her through the birth.

decisions.choice: she did not set her heart: she paid no attention, it did not reach her
decisions.reason: To "set the heart" on something is to take notice of it or take it to heart (2 Samuel 13:20; Psalm 48:14).

decisions.choice: [women]; [to it]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "women", which the Hebrew shows only by the feminine form, and "to it", which English needs after "set her heart".

source.text: וַתִּקְרָ֣א לַנַּ֗עַר אִֽי־כָבוֹד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר גָּלָ֥ה כָב֖וֹד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֶל־הִלָּקַח֙ אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאֶל־חָמִ֖יהָ וְאִישָֽׁהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she called to the boy Ichabod, saying, Has gone into exile glory from Israel, because of [the] taking of [the] ark of the God and because of her father-in-law and her husband.

en.L: And she called the boy Ichabod, saying, "Glory has gone into exile from Israel," because the ark of God was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
en.B: She named the boy Ichabod, saying, "The glory has gone into exile from Israel." She said this because the ark of God had been captured, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
en.R: She named the boy Ichabod, a name that may mean "No glory" or "Where is the glory?" She said, "The glory has left Israel and gone into exile." She said this because the ark of God had been captured, and because her father-in-law and her husband were dead.

fr.L: Et elle appela l’enfant I-Kabod, en disant : « La gloire s’en est allée en exil loin d’Israël », parce que l’arche de Dieu était prise, et à cause de son beau-père et de son mari.
fr.B: Elle appela l’enfant I-Kabod, en disant : « La gloire s’en est allée d’Israël, en exil. » Elle parlait ainsi parce que l’arche de Dieu avait été prise, et à cause de son beau-père et de son mari.
fr.R: Elle a appelé l’enfant I-Kabod, un nom qui peut signifier « Pas de gloire » ou « Où est la gloire ? ». Elle a dit : « La gloire a quitté Israël, elle est partie en exil. » Elle a dit cela parce que l’arche de Dieu avait été prise, et parce que son beau-père et son mari étaient morts.

decisions.choice: Ichabod: a name that plays on "glory", meaning "No glory" or "Where is the glory?"
decisions.reason: The second part of the name is the word "glory". The first part is a short word that can mean "not" (as in Job 22:30, "one who is not innocent") or can ask "where?" (as in the name Jezebel, perhaps "Where is the prince?"). Either way the name says that the glory is gone, and the mother explains it with her words "the glory has gone into exile from Israel". The text does not settle which sense was meant, and both are kept.

decisions.choice: has gone into exile: has been carried away captive, has departed
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for a people taken away into exile (2 Kings 17:23; 25:21). The glory is pictured as a captive led off to a foreign land, as the ark has just been taken into Philistine territory.

decisions.choice: glory: the weighty presence of the LORD that was with the ark
decisions.reason: The LORD's glory filled the tabernacle when it was set up (Exodus 40:34-35), and it was linked with the ark above which he was enthroned (verse 4). To lose the ark is to lose the sign of God's presence among his people. Psalm 78:60-61 looks back on this day: God gave his glory into the hand of the enemy. The word has no article in Hebrew, which gives the saying the force of a proverb.

decisions.choice: because of the taking of the ark ... and because of her father-in-law and her husband: the writer's explanation
decisions.reason: These words give the reasons for the name. The writer names all three losses; in verse 22 she herself speaks only of the ark.

decisions.choice: The glory
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the glory", since English needs the article to make clear that a particular glory, God's, is meant (m3).

decisions.choice: a name that may mean "No glory" or "Where is the glory?"; were dead
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name, keeping both possibilities (m1), so that the reader can see how it connects with her words. It also says what happened to her father-in-law and husband.

decisions.choice: "I-Kabod"
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note writes the name with a hyphen, which shows its two parts, "no" or "where" and "glory", the play the next words explain (m1).

source.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר גָּלָ֥ה כָב֖וֹד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֥י נִלְקַ֖ח אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And she said, Has gone into exile glory from Israel, for has been taken [the] ark of the God.

en.L: And she said, "Glory has gone into exile from Israel, for the ark of God has been taken."
en.B: She said, "The glory has gone into exile from Israel, for the ark of God has been captured."
en.R: She said, "The glory has left Israel and gone into exile, because the ark of God has been captured."

fr.L: Et elle dit : « La gloire s’en est allée en exil loin d’Israël, car l’arche de Dieu a été prise. »
fr.B: Elle dit : « La gloire s’en est allée d’Israël, en exil, car l’arche de Dieu a été prise. »
fr.R: Elle a dit : « La gloire a quitté Israël, elle est partie en exil, parce que l’arche de Dieu a été prise. »

decisions.choice: for the ark of God has been taken: she names only the ark
decisions.reason: She repeats the saying of verse 21, and this time gives one reason only. The loss of God's ark weighs more with her than the deaths in her own family, as it did with Eli (verse 18). The chapter ends on the word "taken".

decisions.choice: the ark in exile: the story continues in chapters 5-6
decisions.reason: The ark goes into the land of the Philistines, where the LORD shows his power against their god Dagon and their cities (chapter 5), until they send it back (chapter 6). The glory has gone into exile, but the LORD has not been defeated.

decisions.choice: The glory
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.
